coverage.evidence: 'peer-ai-eslint-config's settings are in effect ahead of the project's own.' eslint.config.js:21 spreads ...peerAi() after the recommended configs and before the project's own block, so where both set a rule the project's choice wins — docs/standards/ being authoritative. Checked against the computed configuration rather than the source: eslint --print-config on rail.tsx reports 15 peer-ai-prefixed rules in effect. Honest qualification: the duplicate removed from the project's block was @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any, and that rule is still set to error by tseslint.configs.recommended, so TS-02 is covered twice under two names. Harmless, but the one-rule-one-place goal is only partly reached.

'peer-ai doctor no longer reports that nothing enforces TS-02 to TS-09 or REACT-01 to REACT-07 and REACT-11.' Run on this commit, the enforcers warning is gone entirely. In its place doctor reports the two deliberate deferrals, each naming the reason, the work item that ends it and Qudus Lawal as the person who decided: 'TS-07 only reports until ITEM-2 is done' and 'REACT-03 only reports until ITEM-2 is done'. Before this change the same command listed sixteen rules with nothing enforcing them.

'A violation of any newly enforced rule is reported rather than passing silently.' Demonstrated rather than reasoned: an `any` and a non-null assertion were put into rail.tsx and lint reported four errors, including peer-ai-typescript/no-explicit-any and peer-ai-typescript/no-non-null-assertion, both at error severity rather than warning. Errors fail npm run lint and therefore npm run verify. The file was restored and lints clean. This also proves the test exemption is scoped as claimed: the same non-null assertion is an error in source and allowed in a test file.

'A rule left non-blocking is listed in standards.deferred with a reason, who decided it, and the work item that ends the deferral.' peer-ai.config.json:50-66 lists exactly two, TS-07 and REACT-03, each with a reason naming how many findings and where, decidedBy Qudus Lawal, and untilItem ITEM-2. Both read back in doctor's output as 'only reports until ITEM-2 is done'. ITEM-2 exists and its own acceptance criteria include removing both from the deferred list, so the deferral has an end rather than being indefinite.

Beyond the four criteria the item carries only what turning the rules on forced or found. Forced: the react-hooks major upgrade, demanded by peer-ai-eslint-config's peer range, and three plugins its optional peers need. Found and fixed: a floating navigate promise, a progressbar with no accessible name, a setState in an effect, and a config file the linter could not parse. One fix was my own regression, awaiting navigate inside the save's catch, caught in review and corrected. Two test files were added for faults that had none. No feature, screen or behaviour the criteria did not ask for.

Of the four faults fixed, the accessible name has a test proven to fail without it — removing the attribute fails one of five cases and only that one. The remaining two are recorded as an open finding on this item's code review rather than passed over: the use-media-query fix cannot be guarded by a test because it preserved behaviour, demonstrated by running the five new tests against the old implementation and watching all five pass, and the rule that would guard it is ITEM-4's; the navigate separation is unreachable without a route loader.

coverage.reason: No user journey is added or changed. The core journey in the addendum (K1) runs through onboarding, which this item touches only in the order of two statements, and its 21 existing tests pass unchanged. That journey not existing as an end-to-end Playwright test is a project gap, not one this item creates or could close.

coverage.evidence: The rules in scope are tested with plain values, case by case, each named: Rail's proportion at 0.62, above 1 at 1.4, NaN and -0.5, five cases; the hook at matching, not matching, no matchMedia at all, a change event and unmount, five cases. No mock of a module, and the hook's fake is a real event target so a hook that ignored the event would fail.

Both files assert behaviour through the public surface: rail.test.tsx queries by role and accessible name, which is what a screen reader does; use-media-query.test.tsx renders a probe and reads its rendered answer. The one structural assertion, the listener count, checks the documented cleanup PERF-06 requires rather than an internal.

Every claim in this report that could be demonstrated was, by breaking the thing first. Removing aria-label fails one rail case and only that one. Breaking the hook's cleanup fails one case and only that one. Putting an `any` and a non-null assertion into source produces four lint errors. Running the five hook tests against the old setState-in-effect implementation passes all five, which is how the unguarded-fix finding was established rather than guessed. Each was restored and re-run green.

Both new test files import the modules under test by the same relative specifiers the app uses, with no alias or build step between, so what vitest runs is what the bundle contains. The 442 tests and the build both pass in CI on this commit.

The edges in scope are handled and now asserted: a proportion above 1 reports its true value rather than announcing full, NaN and negatives report 0, no matchMedia answers the wide layout, a change event is followed, the listener is removed on unmount, and a save that succeeded followed by a navigation that did not no longer claims the save failed.

findings.title: The import path, which reads an untrusted file and which this change edits, gains no abuse test
findings.evidence: Recorded here as well as on this item's security review, because an acceptance check must not pass over it. The restore handler hands a file's text to importFrom, and an export file is untrusted input. A well-formed foreign file is covered — first-run.test.tsx:400 asserts it is refused and nothing changed — but input shaped to attack is not: a future schemaVersion, a money value as a string, a demo-flagged file restored into a real session, a file truncated mid-object. Issue 106 already records the demo case as real. Validation is schema-based rather than hand-rolled, so this is missing proof rather than a live hole, and it is not a hole this change opened.
findings.fix: Add those cases beside the existing refusal test, each asserting refusal and that the stored snapshot is unchanged. They belong with issue 106, which owns the demo flag and the requirement that it survive every migration step.

summary: Pass. All four acceptance criteria hold and each was demonstrated rather than read: the computed lint configuration shows 15 peer-ai rules in effect, doctor's enforcers warning is gone and replaced by two named deferrals with the owner's name on them, and an injected `any` and non-null assertion produce errors that fail verify. One open finding, carried from the security review: the untrusted import path this change edits has no abuse test. Nothing extra was built.
